MCC Seat Allotment 2026: Your Essential Guide to Medical Admissions

Navigating the Path to Your Dream Medical College

The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) plays a pivotal role in the admission journey for aspiring medical and dental professionals across India. As we look towards MCC Seat Allotment 2026, understanding the intricate process is crucial for candidates aiming for MBBS, BDS, MD, MS, DM, and MCh courses. The MCC is responsible for conducting the centralized online counselling for a significant portion of medical seats, ensuring a transparent and merit-based allocation.

Whether you've cleared NEET UG, NEET PG, or NEET SS, the MCC counselling portal at mcc.nic.in is your gateway to securing a seat in top institutions, including All India Quota (AIQ) seats, Deemed Universities, Central Universities, AIIMS, JIPMER, ESIC, and AFMS colleges.

Key Dates and Expected Schedule for 2026

While official notifications are continuously released, here's an overview of the expected timelines for MCC counselling rounds in 2026, based on current information and previous years' patterns:

Counselling Event NEET UG 2026 (Expected) NEET PG 2026 (Expected) NEET SS 2026 (Actual/Expected)
Result Declaration June 2026 September 2026 (Already declared)
Counselling Schedule Notification July 2026 Feb-March 2026 (for official dates) (Released by March 2026 for Round 1)
Round 1 Registration & Choice Filling Late July / Early August 2026 September 2026 (Completed, Seat Matrix out March 2026)
Round 1 Seat Allotment Result August 2026 October 2026 (Completed)
Round 2 Registration & Choice Filling August / September 2026 October – November 2026 (Follows Round 1)
Mop-Up Round September 2026 December 2026 (Follows Round 2)
Stray Vacancy Round October 2026 February 2026 (Already revised & conducted) (Follows Mop-Up)

Note: Dates for NEET UG 2026 may see slight adjustments due to the re-examination conducted on June 21, 2026. Always refer to the official MCC website (mcc.nic.in) for the most accurate and up-to-date schedule.

The MCC Seat Allotment Process: A Step-by-Step Guide

The MCC counselling process is meticulously designed to ensure fair allocation. Here's a breakdown of the typical steps involved:

1. Online Registration
Candidates must register on the official MCC portal (mcc.nic.in) using their NEET roll number and other personal details. This step is mandatory for participation in the counselling.
2. Payment of Counselling Fee
A non-refundable registration fee and a refundable security deposit are required. The amount varies based on the candidate's category and the type of institution (government vs. deemed universities).
3. Choice Filling & Locking
This is a critical step where candidates select their preferred colleges and courses in order of priority. It is highly recommended to fill in as many choices as possible to maximize your chances. After filling, choices must be locked before the deadline.
4. Seat Allotment Result
The MCC releases the seat allotment results based on NEET rank, category, and filled choices. Candidates can download their provisional allotment letter from the MCC website.
5. Reporting to Allotted College
If allotted a seat, candidates must report to the designated college within the stipulated time for document verification and admission formalities.
6. Upgradation (Optional)
Candidates not satisfied with their Round 1 allotment can opt for upgradation in subsequent rounds. This allows them to participate in further rounds with the possibility of securing a better preferred seat.

Understanding the Seat Matrix

The NEET 2026 Seat Matrix is a vital document released by the MCC before each counselling round. It provides a detailed breakdown of available seats in various colleges, courses (MBBS, BDS, MD, MS, etc.), categories, and quotas.

Studying the seat matrix carefully helps candidates strategize their choice filling, identify colleges with vacancies, and make informed decisions during the counselling process.

Essential Documents Required

Ensure you have the following documents ready for verification:

✅ NEET Admit Card & Scorecard (UG/PG/SS)

✅ Allotment Letter issued by MCC

✅ Class 10th & 12th Mark Sheet and Certificate

✅ MBBS/BDS Degree Certificate (for PG/SS candidates)

✅ Internship Completion Certificate (for PG/SS candidates, by cut-off date)

✅ Permanent/Provisional Registration Certificate (issued by NMC/MCI or State Medical Council)

✅ Valid Photo ID (Aadhaar Card, Passport, etc.)

✅ Category Certificate (OBC/SC/ST/EWS/PwD), if applicable, in central government format

✅ Domicile Certificate (if applying for state quota, though not for AIQ)

Important Tips for a Successful Allotment

✅ **Stay Updated:** Regularly check the official MCC website (mcc.nic.in) for the latest notifications and schedules.

✅ **Research Thoroughly:** Understand colleges, their fee structures, and previous year's cut-offs before choice filling.

✅ **Fill Ample Choices:** Maximize your options by filling 40-50 choices, not just a few.

✅ **Simultaneous State Counselling:** You can participate in both MCC's AIQ counselling and your respective state's counselling.

✅ **Lock Choices Prudently:** Ensure your choice list is final and locked well before the deadline.

✅ **Understand Withdrawal Rules:** Be aware of the rules for withdrawing from an allotted seat to avoid forfeiture of your security deposit.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Q1: Who conducts the MCC counselling?
The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, conducts the online counselling.
Q2: Which seats are covered under MCC counselling?
MCC counsels for 15% All India Quota (AIQ) seats for UG, 50% AIQ seats for PG, and 100% seats in Central Universities, Deemed Universities, AIIMS, JIPMER, ESIC, and AFMS institutions for UG, PG, and SS courses.
Q3: How many rounds are there in MCC counselling?
Typically, MCC counselling is conducted in four rounds: Round 1, Round 2, Mop-Up Round, and Stray Vacancy Round. Some courses may have an additional Special Stray Vacancy Round.
Q4: Can I register for subsequent rounds if I miss Round 1?
Yes, in most cases, fresh registration is allowed for Round 2 and the Mop-Up Round. However, the Stray Vacancy Round usually does not allow new registrations.

The MCC Seat Allotment 2026 is a critical phase in your medical education journey. By staying informed, meticulously following the instructions, and preparing thoroughly, you can significantly enhance your chances of securing a seat in your desired medical or dental college.
